mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < avg(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days by signaling a strengthening labor market and consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above its 3-month moving average AND HOUST > 10th percentile of recent monthly values
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening with rising consumer sentiment
failure_condition: In 20-day windows meeting the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as a contrarian demand signal.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -2% for 2 consecutive months then rises > previous month's level
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon following the pattern, SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be negative due to anticipated inflation pressures and reduced equity risk appetite.
regime_hint: Unexpected inflation surprise in a neutral policy environment
failure_condition: In 20-day windows after the CPI surprise, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% for two consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as a signal of tightening labor market conditions and higher risk aversion.
failure_condition: During the 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not negative or are indistinguishable from baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payrolls (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (HOUST) above their respective 5th percentile monthly thresholds for three consecutive months predict a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to dual labor and demand strength.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 5th percentile of last 12 months AND HOUST > 5th percentile of last 12 months for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20-day windows meeting the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling retail sales proxies (not available in the catalog; fallback: persistent monthly declines in industrial production (INDPRO) for 4 months) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as a supply shock warning.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window following the 4-month decline, SPX 60-day forward returns are not negative or are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 2% for the first time in a 12-month window, the S&P 500 forward 5-day return tends to be positive as markets anticipate further easing and liquidity injection.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS < 2% for the first time in the last 12 months
regime_hint: First sign of easing in a restrictive cycle
failure_condition: During the 5-day window following the trigger, SPX 5-day forward returns are not positive or are not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).
